# statuspal-next_status_page (Resource)

Manages a StatusPal Next status page.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "statuspal-next_status_page" "acme" {
  name        = "Acme Status"
  subdomain   = "acme-status"
  timezone    = "America/New_York"
  website_url = "https://acme.com"

  require_authentication = false

  notification_settings = {
    email_enabled    = true
    slack_enabled    = false
    rss_feed_enabled = true
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name of the status page.
- `subdomain` (String) Subdomain that addresses the status page (e.g. `acme-status`). Changing it forces a new resource, because the API addresses the page by subdomain.
- `timezone` (String) Primary timezone used to display incidents (e.g. `America/New_York`).
- `website_url` (String) URL of the company, project, or service this page reports on.

### Optional

- `notification_settings` (Attributes) Subscriber notification channels for this status page. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--notification_settings))
- `require_authentication` (Boolean) When `true`, only signed-in members can view the status page.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Timestamp at which the status page was created.
- `current_status` (String) Derived overall status: `operational`, `degraded`, or `unavailable`.
- `id` (String) Server-generated identifier of the status page.
- `updated_at` (String) Timestamp at which the status page was last updated.

<a id="nestedatt--notification_settings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `notification_settings`

Optional:

- `email_enabled` (Boolean) Allow subscribers to receive email notifications.
- `rss_feed_enabled` (Boolean) Expose an RSS/Atom feed of updates.
- `slack_enabled` (Boolean) Allow subscribers to subscribe via Slack.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# Status pages are imported by subdomain.
terraform import statuspal-next_status_page.acme acme-status
```
